transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Khan, Diego Ramos, Maya Patel (Redwood); Liam O'Connor, Priya Menon, Evan Chen, Sofia Alvarez (Tidal Retail)

Summary:
- QBR / health check focused on usage, cost trends, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment.
- Tidal is approaching a threshold where dedicated capacity / reserved commit is being considered to control unit cost and tail latency.
- Action items: benchmarks, pricing, and SOC2/VPC docs to be shared.

00:00 Aisha Khan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call, and then we'll go through the usage and cost trends, reliability, and then roadmap alignment.
00:18 Liam O'Connor: Yep, Liam here for Tidal. Priya's on, Evan, Sofia also here.
00:25 Aisha Khan: Great. Diego from SE will cover the latency stuff and Maya will cover the invoicing and contract options.
00:34 Priya Menon: Thanks. High level — we're happy with the model quality, but cost has crept up and the 99th tail has been... yeah, a little painful during peak campaigns.
00:46 Diego Ramos: Right, we've been looking at your token distribution. Looks like a mix of a lot of short queries and some long invoice generation prompts that spike the seq len. That combination is biting on batching and K V cache efficiency.
01:03 Evan Chen: Just to be clear, during Black Friday style loads our 99p goes from 480ms to 1.2s on the hosted endpoints, and cost pulses by ~2.2x.
01:15 Diego Ramos: Mm-hmm. So there are a couple levers: 1) dedicated pools to avoid noisy neighbor variability; 2) quantized model variants for the long sequences; 3) prefix caching for repeated prompts.
01:28 Sofia Alvarez: Can Redwood do model pinning + canary rollouts if we move to dedicated? We need to control drift to avoid regressions in NPS.
01:35 Aisha Khan: Yes — we support pinning and canary/A B rollouts, and quality regressions can be tied to eval sets. We'll share the rollout docs.
01:44 Priya Menon: On security — we need V P C peering, K M S integration for key management, and of course SOC two artifacts. Also SSO SAML, RBAC for roles.
01:58 Maya Patel: We have an enterprise package that covers VPC private deployments and KMS/HSM integrations. I'll attach the SOC 2 report and the VPC network diagram. Sorry — sometimes the transcriber writes Sam L for SAML, so apologies if the notes look odd.
02:12 Liam O'Connor: No worries. For compliance we also need audit logs retention for 13 months, and the ability to get per-route token usage for cost allocation.
02:22 Maya Patel: We can do token-level breakdowns per route — the console exposes that and we can also export for your billing system.
02:30 Evan Chen: A question on failover — if we route to a lower-cost model variant in a region outage, what's the expected degradation? We can't have checkout latency jump too much.
02:42 Diego Ramos: We'll define SLOs and fallback policies. Typically fallback to a smaller model increases latency slightly and may change output quality. We can set automatic fallback thresholds, plus human-on-call alerts. We'll test with a staged failover.
02:58 Sofia Alvarez: One of our concerns — embeddings cost is getting large for similarity search. We're seeing renewed usage for near real-time product recs. Any guidance?
03:10 Aisha Khan: For embeddings we recommend batched upserts and TTL-based caching for near-term recency. Also consider quantized embedding indices and incremental updates to reduce unit costs. We'll share Optimize recommendations.
03:26 Priya Menon: Can you show the cost trend slide?
03:30 Maya Patel: (screen share noted) In January to February you had a 28% month-over-month increase driven by more embed usage and a spike in long-run document summarizations. The per-token effective price went up because of those longer sequences.
03:46 Liam O'Connor: Is there a simple threshold where reserved capacity makes sense? We want to avoid over committing.
03:52 Maya Patel: Typically, customers cross over at sustained throughput where monthly committed spend is 20-25% above current hosted runrate but gets you 40-60% better unit economics. We'll run a sizing calc for your 30k req/day profile.
04:10 Evan Chen: On reliability: last month we saw two incidents, one was a region blip in us-west2 and another was a degraded health check — both recovered, but we lost some telemetry. Can we get deeper post-mortem?
04:24 Diego Ramos: I'll pull the incident logs and share the root cause. It looks like the first was a transient infra scheduler issue on the provider side; the second was a misconfigured health-check threshold.
04:34 Priya Menon: We would like email alerts for incidents and a pager integration for Sev1s.
04:40 Maya Patel: We have PagerDuty integration and can add route-based alerting.
04:46 Aisha Khan: Recap so far: 1) we'll run benchmarks, 2) Maya will send pricing/commit options and SOC 2 + V P C docs, 3) Diego will share incident logs and run latency experiments, 4) Tidal to share peak logs.
05:01 Sofia Alvarez: One small nit — some model outputs have slight hallucinations on certain SKU descriptions, that's caused downstream classification mismatches.
05:12 Diego Ramos: We can work with you on prompt templates and small evals to catch regressions. Also can try a slightly larger context window model for those SKU prompts or constraint generation with structured output.
05:28 Liam O'Connor: Timeline — we're deciding by end of month if we want a reserved commit for Q2. So we'd need the detailed pricing and the benchmark by next week to make the case.
05:40 Maya Patel: Understood, we'll prioritize the pricing and the deck.
05:46 Priya Menon: On networking, can Redwood support private on-prem connectors for air-gapped use? We have a regulated sub-division that might need that later this year.
05:58 Aisha Khan: Yes, our Private deployment supports on-prem packages and offline connectors; we'll include the options in the docs.
06:06 Evan Chen: A couple of technical deep dive asks: 1) what kernels / accelerations are used for long sequence attention? 2) how does KV cache eviction work with long-lived sessions?
06:20 Diego Ramos: Short answers: we use a mix of attention kernel selection depending on seq len, and runtime picks quantized paths when available. For KV cache we have eviction policies that prefer prefix caching for reused context, and you can tune cache TTL per route — we can set up an SE call to dig into this.
06:40 Priya Menon: Let's schedule that SE deep dive after the sizing call.
06:45 Aisha Khan: Sounds good.
06:48 (transcription noise) Speaker 1: uh-huh, yeah.
06:52 Sofia Alvarez: Quick question on data retention — do you store raw prompts by default?
06:57 Maya Patel: By default hosted endpoints retain minimal logs for 30 days; enterprise private options support customizable retention and no-logs policies.
07:08 Liam O'Connor: OK that's fine.
07:11 Aisha Khan: Let's do a short run through of the proposed timeline: Diego runs benchmarks this week, Maya sends pricing by Friday, SE sizing call early next week, then a decision by end of month.
07:26 Priya Menon: Agreed.
07:29 Diego Ramos: I'll also include a sample benchmark script, but heads up the transcriber sometimes writes K V as separate letters "K V" so don't mind that in the notes.
07:40 Evan Chen: Any blockers on our side? We need to extract the peak logs and share them — Liam will own that.
07:47 Liam O'Connor: Yep I'll pull them and get to Maya by Sunday.
07:51 Aisha Khan: Great. Any final questions?
07:54 Sofia Alvarez: None from me.
07:56 Priya Menon: No.
07:58 Aisha Khan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with deck, pricing, and benchmark results.
08:03 (end)
